topics.title: Vectors and Translation
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Define translation with a vector. (k, u, s)
Represent vectors both single and combined geometrically. (u, s)

body.text: A scalar is a quantity with size only, such as 5 kg or 20°C. A vector has both size (magnitude) and direction, such as "3 km east". A translation slides every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction without turning or resizing it — a vector describes exactly that slide.

A column vector is written (a, b) stacked vertically, where a is the movement parallel to the x-axis (positive = right) and b is the movement parallel to the y-axis (positive = up). The vector that translates point (1, 2) to point (4, -1) is found by subtracting: (4-1, -1-2) = (3, -3).

Combining two translations means adding their column vectors component by component. Translating a point first by (2, 3) then by (-5, 1) has the same overall effect as one translation by (2+(-5), 3+1) = (-3, 4).
